turns.replyText:
Honestly, is the pricier one worth the extra, or is the cheaper one fine?
The cheaper option—the Freeze Dried Vegetable Kit ($40.70)—is completely fine and a great value if you primarily want quick, crunchable snacks or easy salad toppings without any preparation.
The pricier Kitchen/Cooking Kit ($60.44) is worth the extra $19.74 if you plan to cook meals, soups, or stews. It includes 8 pouches instead of 5, providing more total volume and a wider variety of core cooking staples like potatoes, sweet potatoes, carrots, celery, and cabbage.
If you just want a light, healthy snack, stick with the $40.70 kit. If you want ingredients to build full meals and stretch your grocery budget, the $60.44 kit gives you better versatility.
